title: arXiv Mathematics — 13 November 2026: 9 notable recent papers
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-recent-paper ranking, not measured popularity. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old, and Semantic Scholar citation fields were not usable for this snapshot.

sections.title: The Pólya--Szegő buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
sections.abstract: The authors prove the Pólya--Szegő volume-minimization conjecture for the first clamped buckling eigenvalue in dimensions 2 through 47, with a sharp comparison to the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and a capacity-qualified equality class.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove, for every open set Ω in Rⁿ of finite positive volume and 2 ≤ n ≤ 47, Λ₁(Ω) ≥ (jₙ/₂,₁ / jₙ/₂₋₁,₁)² λ₁ᴰ(Ω); Faber--Krahn yields the ball-minimizing volume bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Open subsets of Euclidean n-space, finite positive volume, dimensions 2--47; equality in the volume inequality permits removal of a relatively closed set of zero H²-capacity.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors' calibration fails for n ≥ 48; this does not disprove the conjecture there. The preprint's proof has not been independently verified here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: MathWorld's buckling-conjecture entry, updated 14 Nov, discusses and cites this dimension-2-to-47 extension; the AIM problem page separately tracks the planar conjecture and its prior Lean-verified resolution. The explicit dimension range and method boundary strengthen its significance signal.

sections.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
sections.abstract: The authors construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space with a logarithmic-capacity-zero radial zero set whose polynomial multiples are not dense, claiming a counterexample to the Brown--Shields conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors state that they disprove the conjecture by constructing an outer f in the Dirichlet space with radial zero set of logarithmic capacity zero but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate 1; their main theorem gives a positive lower bound for the approximation error.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The classical holomorphic Dirichlet space on the unit disk; outerness and the radial boundary zero set are understood in that setting.
sections.unique_caveat: A contemporaneous MathWorld note says independent specialist review of the complete proof had not been reported; treat the counterexample as an author claim pending scrutiny.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: MathWorld's Brown--Shields entry was updated 13 Nov and discusses this exact preprint, an immediate independent, topic-specific discussion of a longstanding conjecture. The external note distinguishes the claimed refutation from a reviewed resolution.

sections.title: Prime values of linear forms and a quadratic form: one proof and two arithmetic applications
sections.abstract: Using higher-order Fourier analysis, the authors prove simultaneous prime values for suitable systems of linear forms and an imaginary-quadratic norm form, derive a Bateman--Horn-type asymptotic, and apply it to weak approximation and quadratic twists of elliptic curves.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem A gives an asymptotic prime-counting formula and infinitely many simultaneous prime values when the singular series is positive; applications establish new Brauer--Manin weak-approximation cases and infinitely many quadratic twists in a family of rank exactly two.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The homogeneous parts of the linear forms must be pairwise linearly independent; the quadratic form is a norm from an imaginary quadratic field in the specified integral-linear-coordinate form; local obstructions must be absent for infinitude.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated prime theorem is for this norm-form family, not arbitrary binary quadratic forms; the authors identify broader forms as a possible generalization rather than a result established here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A substantial 74-page result connects analytic number theory to arithmetic geometry in two concrete applications. Placement rests on the explicit theorem and cross-area relevance, rather than measured readership.

sections.title: Macroscopic L-infinity bounds for the homogeneous Landau--Coulomb equation
sections.abstract: For smooth, rapidly decaying solutions of the three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential, the authors prove positive-time global L-infinity bounds depending only on initial mass, momentum, energy and entropy, resolving a previously posed regularization problem.
sections.claimed_result: For every 0 < τ < T, the authors bound the global velocity-space L-infinity norm on τ ≤ t ≤ T by C(H, τ, T), for the normalized smooth, rapidly decaying solutions described in the paper.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Three-dimensional spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb interaction; an a priori estimate for smooth, rapidly decaying solutions, with constants controlled by macroscopic conserved quantities and initial entropy.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper says upgrading this estimate to global existence for general finite-mass, energy and entropy data needs an approximation and initial-trace stability argument, which it does not pursue.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract identifies a specific open problem and a strong theorem with substantially weaker data requirements than earlier estimates; the technical scope is concrete and directly stated in the paper.

sections.title: The coercivity conjecture for nonlocal energies
sections.abstract: The authors show that uniform ellipticity does not generally imply H-s-coercivity for symmetric nonlocal kernels, while proving coercivity under several cancellation or geometric assumptions and deriving regularity consequences.
sections.claimed_result: The authors give counterexamples whenever n > 2s, prove the conjecture for n = 1 and s > 1/2, establish a local coercivity criterion based on annular cancellation, and derive Hölder estimates under ellipticity and cancellation hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Symmetric nonlocal kernels of order 2s, 0 < s < 1; counterexamples include smooth compactly supported test functions, and positive criteria require the stated cancellation or nonconcentration conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated failure and positive range leave the borderline n = 2s unspecified; conclusions for other kernels depend on additional cancellation or geometric assumptions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper overturns a broad conjecture in a sharply delineated parameter range and replaces it with a local criterion applicable to important kernel classes, including a non-cutoff Boltzmann setting; implications span nonlocal PDE regularity and kinetic estimates.

sections.title: Rational isogenies of of rank-two Drinfeld modules
sections.abstract: The authors determine rational points on Drinfeld modular curves of arbitrary level over F_q(T), obtaining a classification of rational cyclic isogenies and consequences for torsion, isogeny-class size and automorphism groups.
sections.claimed_result: The authors classify rational cyclic isogenies of rank-two Drinfeld F_q[T]-modules over F_q(T), prove Schweizer's conjecture on rational torsion, and determine geometric automorphism groups of X_0(p) for primes p of degree at least three.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Rank-two Drinfeld modules over the rational function field F_q(T), with rational points on Drinfeld modular curves X_0(n) for arbitrary level n.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification is specific to rank two over F_q(T); the abstract does not claim a classification over general global function fields or in higher rank.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The submission combines two mathematical subject classes and claims a complete classification plus a named conjecture resolution, with further uniform bounds and geometric consequences.

sections.title: Asymptotically Optimal Bounds for Counting Near-Minimum Circuits in Regular Matroids
sections.abstract: The authors improve the bound on the number of near-minimum-weight circuits in a regular matroid to (Km)^(2 alpha), resolve a recent conjecture for parallel basis search, and obtain consequences for regular codes and totally unimodular lattices.
sections.claimed_result: For positive weights and weighted girth g_w, the circuit count at weight at most alpha g_w is bounded by (Km)^(2 alpha); asymptotic optimality is conditional on the Erdős girth conjecture for all real alpha and unconditional for half-integer alpha.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Regular matroids on m elements, positive element weights and real alpha ≥ 1.
sections.unique_caveat: Full asymptotic optimality for arbitrary real alpha is conditional on the Erdős girth conjecture; the unconditional optimality statement is limited to half-integer alpha.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The new exponent improves a previous m^O(alpha^2) bound, the authors resolve a recent algorithmic conjecture, and the result cross-lists discrete mathematics while yielding coding and lattice applications.

sections.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
sections.abstract: For each superdiffusive memory parameter, the authors prove that the initial biases producing a bimodal limit density form a proper open interval, establishing a conjecture and a unique memory threshold for its nonemptiness.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove unimodality for sufficiently biased starts and exactly two local maxima for biases inside a proper open interval; the interval is nonempty precisely above one memory threshold, numerically about 0.6688.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The superdiffusive elephant random walk; the shape statement concerns the limiting density as a function of initial bias.
sections.unique_caveat: The threshold is characterized uniquely but reported numerically in the abstract; the results concern the superdiffusive regime, not every memory parameter.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper settles a stated conjecture, gives a precise interval-and-threshold characterization, and its arXiv comments list code, certificates and Lean files; the probability/statistical-mechanics cross-list adds another checkable relevance signal.

sections.title: Random Chowla and Goldbach Conjectures
sections.abstract: For Rademacher random multiplicative functions and polynomials with positive square-free-value density, the authors prove a normalized Gaussian limit; they also establish random Goldbach-type results for selected bivariate functions and settings.
sections.claimed_result: For each non-linear integer polynomial P with positive square-free-value density, the normalized sum of a Rademacher random multiplicative function along P(n) converges in distribution to a standard Gaussian; the paper also proves analogous statements for selected random Goldbach-type sums.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The polynomial must have positive density of square-free values; the Chowla-type result is for Rademacher random multiplicative functions, while Goldbach-type conclusions apply to a suitable class of bivariate functions and only special Rademacher cases.
sections.unique_caveat: These are random analogues and do not prove the classical deterministic Chowla or Goldbach conjectures; the polynomial and bivariate-function hypotheses are essential.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Its three-way number-theory/combinatorics/probability cross-list and method-of-moments theorem connect probabilistic number theory with random additive problems; breadth, rather than citation growth, supports its placement.
